clusters.title: Russell Brand Convicted of Rape and Sexual Assault in London
clusters.summary: Russell Brand, a British comedian and actor, was found guilty by a London jury of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The charges stemmed from incidents involving four women between 2005 and 2009. Brand was acquitted of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault. He denied the allegations, claiming he never forced anyone against their will.

event_overview.title: About Ukraine-Russia Ceasefire
event_overview.subject: Ukraine-Russia Ceasefire
event_overview.summary: The Ukraine-Russia ceasefire refers to efforts to halt fighting between Ukraine and the Russian Federation during the wider war, including limited, temporary or geographically defined pauses as well as proposals for a nationwide cessation of hostilities. Such arrangements are generally framed as an initial de-escalation measure rather than a final political settlement of the conflict.

facts.label: Conflict dates
facts.value: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine began on February 24, 2022; the United Nations also places the wider aggression against Ukraine in a context extending back to 2014.

facts.label: Parties and geography
facts.value: The principal parties are Ukraine and the Russian Federation; proposed ceasefires concern fighting on Ukrainian territory and may address land, air and maritime operations rather than a single battlefield.

facts.label: Purpose and scope
facts.value: Recent diplomatic formulations have described a full ceasefire as immediate and unconditional, intended to stop hostilities and create space for negotiations toward a broader peace; Ukraine and several European partners proposed a minimum 30-day ceasefire in May 2025 across air, sea and land.

facts.label: International role
facts.value: The United Nations has called for a full, immediate and unconditional ceasefire as a first step toward a just, lasting and comprehensive peace, while noting that the United States facilitated a May 2026 temporary ceasefire and planned prisoner exchange.

facts.label: Legal context
facts.value: UN resolutions and statements emphasize Ukraine’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders; the UN General Assembly has held that attempted territorial changes achieved through force have no validity under international law.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the late-October to early-November 2026 localized-ceasefire discussions and related U.S.-hosted engagement, not the full military, diplomatic or humanitarian history of the Russia-Ukraine war.

event_overview.title: About India Elections
event_overview.subject: India Elections
event_overview.summary: India’s elections are administered by the Election Commission of India (ECI), a permanent constitutional body responsible for electoral rolls and for conducting elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of president and vice-president. The referenced protests concern political pressure directed at the leadership of that institution; the underlying issue is the governance and perceived independence of the national election authority rather than a separate electoral contest.

facts.label: Constitutional mandate
facts.value: Article 324 of the Constitution places the superintendence, direction and control of electoral-roll preparation and elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the president and vice-president with the Election Commission of India.

facts.label: Institutional structure
facts.value: The ECI consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners; it has operated as a multi-member commission since 1993, with decisions made by majority vote.

facts.label: Appointment and term
facts.value: Under the 2023 statute, the president appoints commissioners on the recommendation of a selection committee comprising the prime minister, the Lok Sabha opposition leader (or leader of the largest opposition party if no opposition leader is recognized), and a Union cabinet minister nominated by the prime minister. The term is six years or until age 65, whichever comes first, with no reappointment.

facts.label: Removal protections
facts.value: The chief election commissioner may be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge; other election commissioners may be removed only on the chief election commissioner’s recommendation.

facts.label: Electoral scope
facts.value: The ECI administers national and state-level elections, including elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and state legislative assemblies, as well as presidential and vice-presidential elections. The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years, although it may be dissolved earlier.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline captures the September 25, 2026 protest development involving India’s election leadership, but it does not provide a comprehensive record of India’s electoral administration, legal disputes, election results, or the unrelated protest developments listed for Spain and France.

story_report.summary: Thousands of pupils, university students and teachers marched through central Athens on Nov. 5, pressing for better-funded schools as part of a nationwide education campaign. The action followed demonstrations in more than 50 Greek cities on Oct. 21 over funding, staffing, pay, living costs and student housing. The secondary-teachers’ federation, OLME, called a four-hour work stoppage to enable teachers to join the Athens protest, extending organized pressure on the government over school and university conditions.

sections.heading: Education Spending and School Conditions
sections.body: Protesters’ calls for increased funding are set against official figures showing Greece allocated 8.0% of total public spending to education, below the EU average of 9.6% and among the bloc’s lowest shares. OLME says schools lack sufficient funding, staff and infrastructure, while education-related costs for families are rising. Demonstrators also sought building inspections and repairs, permanent appointments to fill vacancies and smaller classes.

sections.heading: Student Housing and Education Access
sections.body: Student groups and unions say high rents and limited dormitory capacity are making study unaffordable, and have called for new residences, rent support and better free meals. Greece’s Constitution provides for free education at state institutions, including university-level education through self-governed public-law institutions. The Education Ministry says it has raised funding for the student-housing allowance from €51 million in 2019 to €90 million in 2026 and has more than €733 million in residence projects under way.

sections.heading: Government Plans and Continuing Mobilization
sections.body: The ministry has announced a planned Panteion University student residence by May 2027 and upgrades to existing facilities, but those measures do not constitute acceptance of the protesters’ wider platform. Separately, OLME authorized three-hour stoppages from Nov. 2 to 30 in a dispute over teacher-evaluation rules. Before the October protests, To Vima reported that student associations and unions were considering further escalation, including possible nationwide strike action in November.

event_overview.title: About Football Tragedy
event_overview.subject: Football Tragedy
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda, a 30-year-old CD Tenerife forward, after a serious on-field collision during a match against FC Andorra in Spain. He was treated at the stadium and taken to hospital, where he died on November 3, 2026; the incident prompted tributes and competition postponements across Spanish and European football.

facts.label: Date and player
facts.value: CD Tenerife announced that Jesús de Miguel Alameda died at 8:00 a.m. on November 3, 2026. The Royal Spanish Football Federation identified him as a CD Tenerife player.

facts.label: Match context
facts.value: The fatal incident followed a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono in a Spanish second-division match at Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López; the match was abandoned after medical personnel entered the field.

facts.label: Medical and investigative context
facts.value: Reporting said de Miguel suffered cardiac arrest after the collision and was hospitalized in intensive care. Spanish police opened an investigation, reported as being under judicial supervision; no finding of legal responsibility is established by those reports.

facts.label: Spanish football response
facts.value: The RFEF initially postponed Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina fixtures scheduled for November 3, then extended the suspension of its competitions through November 5 as a mark of respect.

facts.label: Wider commemoration
facts.value: UEFA said a moment of silence would be held at its matches that week, while the RFEF, LALIGA and Liga F announced coordinated tributes for fixtures from November 6 to 9.

event_overview.title: About India Elections
event_overview.subject: India Elections
event_overview.summary: India’s elections are administered by the Election Commission of India (ECI), a permanent constitutional body responsible for electoral rolls and for conducting elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of president and vice-president. The referenced protests concern political pressure directed at the leadership of that institution; the underlying issue is the governance and perceived independence of the national election authority rather than a separate electoral contest.

facts.label: Constitutional mandate
facts.value: Article 324 of the Constitution places the superintendence, direction and control of electoral-roll preparation and elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the president and vice-president with the Election Commission of India.

facts.label: Institutional structure
facts.value: The ECI consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners; it has operated as a multi-member commission since 1993, with decisions made by majority vote.

facts.label: Appointment and term
facts.value: Under the 2023 statute, the president appoints commissioners on the recommendation of a selection committee comprising the prime minister, the Lok Sabha opposition leader (or leader of the largest opposition party if no opposition leader is recognized), and a Union cabinet minister nominated by the prime minister. The term is six years or until age 65, whichever comes first, with no reappointment.

facts.label: Removal protections
facts.value: The chief election commissioner may be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge; other election commissioners may be removed only on the chief election commissioner’s recommendation.

facts.label: Electoral scope
facts.value: The ECI administers national and state-level elections, including elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and state legislative assemblies, as well as presidential and vice-presidential elections. The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years, although it may be dissolved earlier.

event_overview.title: About India Elections
event_overview.subject: India Elections
event_overview.summary: India’s elections are administered by the Election Commission of India (ECI), a permanent constitutional body responsible for electoral rolls and for conducting elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of president and vice-president. The referenced protests concern political pressure directed at the leadership of that institution; the underlying issue is the governance and perceived independence of the national election authority rather than a separate electoral contest.

facts.label: Constitutional mandate
facts.value: Article 324 of the Constitution places the superintendence, direction and control of electoral-roll preparation and elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the president and vice-president with the Election Commission of India.

facts.label: Institutional structure
facts.value: The ECI consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners; it has operated as a multi-member commission since 1993, with decisions made by majority vote.

facts.label: Appointment and term
facts.value: Under the 2023 statute, the president appoints commissioners on the recommendation of a selection committee comprising the prime minister, the Lok Sabha opposition leader (or leader of the largest opposition party if no opposition leader is recognized), and a Union cabinet minister nominated by the prime minister. The term is six years or until age 65, whichever comes first, with no reappointment.

facts.label: Removal protections
facts.value: The chief election commissioner may be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge; other election commissioners may be removed only on the chief election commissioner’s recommendation.

facts.label: Electoral scope
facts.value: The ECI administers national and state-level elections, including elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and state legislative assemblies, as well as presidential and vice-presidential elections. The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years, although it may be dissolved earlier.

event_overview.title: About Vaccine Trials
event_overview.subject: Vaccine Trials
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a proposed randomized clinical trial of a hepatitis B birth-dose vaccine among newborns in Guinea-Bissau, led by the Bandim Health Project and supported through a U.S. CDC award. The study became controversial because it would compare vaccination at birth with vaccination beginning under the country’s existing routine schedule, while WHO said that withholding a proven birth-dose intervention from some newborns was ethically and scientifically unjustified.

facts.label: Proposed design
facts.value: The protocol described a single-blind, multicenter phase IV randomized controlled trial enrolling healthy newborns younger than one week, assigned 1:1 either to receive monovalent hepatitis B vaccine at birth with BCG and oral polio vaccine or to receive only BCG and oral polio vaccine at birth.

facts.label: Planned scale and location
facts.value: Researchers aimed to recruit at least 14,500 children over two years, beginning at Hospital Nacional Simão Mendes and potentially expanding to other facilities in the greater Bissau area.

facts.label: Stated purpose and U.S. support
facts.value: The CDC award described the purpose as evaluating neonatal monovalent hepatitis B vaccination’s effects on early-life mortality, morbidity, and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes through a randomized trial in Guinea-Bissau.

facts.label: National immunization context
facts.value: WHO said Guinea-Bissau formally decided in 2024 to add a hepatitis B birth dose to its national schedule, with introduction planned by 2028; the country’s routine program had not yet provided that dose at birth.

facts.label: Ethical and regulatory context
facts.value: WHO stated in February 2026 that, as publicly described, the trial was inconsistent with established ethical and scientific principles and noted that Guinea-Bissau had suspended it pending technical review. Reporting on November 5 said the project had subsequently failed to obtain necessary government approval and would not move forward in Guinea-Bissau, although public official detail on the final action was limited

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the trial’s reported October 2026 movement toward implementation and its reported November halt, not the full history of hepatitis B vaccination policy, the wider Bandim Health Project, or every ethics and regulatory review.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct hostilities between the United States and Iran, following a wider regional escalation that had included Israeli strikes and Iranian attacks against regional targets. Fighting has been closely tied to the security of commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s missile and nuclear capabilities, and negotiations over a ceasefire and longer-term nonproliferation arrangements.

facts.label: Start and setting
facts.value: The major 2026 phase of the conflict began on February 28, 2026, with U.S. and Israeli military action against Iran followed by Iranian attacks affecting states across the Gulf region.

facts.label: Principal parties
facts.value: The direct conflict and ceasefire diplomacy have principally involved the United States and Iran, while Israel, Gulf states and armed groups aligned with Iran have been important regional actors.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: Hostilities and their effects have extended beyond Iran to the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, including threats to military facilities and commercial vessels near Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Iranian coastal areas.

facts.label: Ceasefire and diplomacy
facts.value: A U.S.-Iran ceasefire was announced on April 7, 2026 and later extended; a June 17 memorandum of understanding provided for cessation of hostilities, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations toward a broader agreement. The arrangements remained fragile amid subsequent maritime incidents and renewed strikes.

facts.label: Nuclear and legal context
facts.value: The conflict is linked to long-running international concerns over Iran’s nuclear program and safeguards access. The IAEA reported that attacks and Iran’s suspension of cooperation severely reduced its ability to verify nuclear material and facilities; in the United States, Congress has also debated the President’s authority to conduct hostilities against Iran under the War Powers Resolution.

event_overview.title: About India Elections
event_overview.subject: India Elections
event_overview.summary: India’s elections are administered by the Election Commission of India (ECI), a permanent constitutional body responsible for electoral rolls and for conducting elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of president and vice-president. The referenced protests concern political pressure directed at the leadership of that institution; the underlying issue is the governance and perceived independence of the national election authority rather than a separate electoral contest.

facts.label: Constitutional mandate
facts.value: Article 324 of the Constitution places the superintendence, direction and control of electoral-roll preparation and elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the president and vice-president with the Election Commission of India.

facts.label: Institutional structure
facts.value: The ECI consists of a Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners; it has operated as a multi-member commission since 1993, with decisions made by majority vote.

facts.label: Appointment and term
facts.value: Under the 2023 statute, the president appoints commissioners on the recommendation of a selection committee comprising the prime minister, the Lok Sabha opposition leader (or leader of the largest opposition party if no opposition leader is recognized), and a Union cabinet minister nominated by the prime minister. The term is six years or until age 65, whichever comes first, with no reappointment.

facts.label: Removal protections
facts.value: The chief election commissioner may be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge; other election commissioners may be removed only on the chief election commissioner’s recommendation.

facts.label: Electoral scope
facts.value: The ECI administers national and state-level elections, including elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and state legislative assemblies, as well as presidential and vice-presidential elections. The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years, although it may be dissolved earlier.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers to the 2026 armed conflict centered on direct hostilities between the United States and Iran, following a wider regional escalation that had included Israeli strikes and Iranian attacks against regional targets. Fighting has been closely tied to the security of commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran’s missile and nuclear capabilities, and negotiations over a ceasefire and longer-term nonproliferation arrangements.

facts.label: Start and setting
facts.value: The major 2026 phase of the conflict began on February 28, 2026, with U.S. and Israeli military action against Iran followed by Iranian attacks affecting states across the Gulf region.

facts.label: Principal parties
facts.value: The direct conflict and ceasefire diplomacy have principally involved the United States and Iran, while Israel, Gulf states and armed groups aligned with Iran have been important regional actors.

facts.label: Geographic scope
facts.value: Hostilities and their effects have extended beyond Iran to the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, including threats to military facilities and commercial vessels near Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Iranian coastal areas.

facts.label: Ceasefire and diplomacy
facts.value: A U.S.-Iran ceasefire was announced on April 7, 2026 and later extended; a June 17 memorandum of understanding provided for cessation of hostilities, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and negotiations toward a broader agreement. The arrangements remained fragile amid subsequent maritime incidents and renewed strikes.

facts.label: Nuclear and legal context
facts.value: The conflict is linked to long-running international concerns over Iran’s nuclear program and safeguards access. The IAEA reported that attacks and Iran’s suspension of cooperation severely reduced its ability to verify nuclear material and facilities; in the United States, Congress has also debated the President’s authority to conduct hostilities against Iran under the War Powers Resolution.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on late-July 2026 escalation involving threats to Iranian infrastructure, Strait of Hormuz shipping, congressional war-powers action, oil-market effects, Houthi activity and renewed ceasefire talks; it does not provide a complete military, humanitarian, diplomatic or legal history of the conflict before or after that period.
